given: a stock record already exists for a given SKU at a given location
when: the operator files stock again for that same (SKU, location) pair
then: the existing record is updated in place with the newly filed values, exactly one record for that pair remains, no duplicate record is created, and no error page is shown

independence.rationale: AC1 and AC2 cover a first-time write of a new record; this covers the write-collision path where the pair already exists. The collision outcome (update in place, single authoritative record, no duplicate, no error) is independently breakable: a build could correctly create first records yet duplicate or error on a repeat filing, failing this AC while AC1 and AC2 stay green.

architectural_notes: API-layer AC on the filing boundary (app/routes) -> stock service (app/services) -> stock repository (app/repositories). The single-record-per-pair guarantee rests on the DB-level unique (sku, location) constraint (PI1); the repository realizes the write-collision path as an idempotent upsert so a repeat filing updates in place rather than inserting a duplicate or surfacing an error. The service owns the transactional boundary for the read-or-create decision; conflict handling is a repository/schema concern, never the boundary. Verified by a real-branch integration test asserting exactly one row remains after a repeat filing.
